objective: Add a read-only realtime Resource Monitor page to the Electron operator dashboard that reports truthful physical RAM/VRAM telemetry, shared-scheduler reservations and leases, loaded or unloaded local/cloud model state, bounded transition history, and plain-Vietnamese headroom analysis while preserving the M08 perception architecture and local safety boundaries.
non_goals: Do not allow the dashboard to start, stop, load, unload or reconfigure models in this slice.
Do not run shell commands, process inspection, persistence or network access from the sandboxed Vue renderer.
Do not claim Windows WDDM per-process VRAM values when NVIDIA does not expose them.
Do not add background telemetry persistence, raw command logs, chat content, screen pixels or API credentials.
Do not open a new product module or run repeat, soak, frozen-SHA or full release verification.
contracts: The renderer receives resource data only through an operator-only typed preload IPC channel; it has no direct child_process, os, filesystem, persistence or network access.
The control-plane resource route is loopback-only, read-only, bounded and returns no API key, prompt, chat content, screen pixel, owner path or arbitrary process command line.
Physical RAM/VRAM measurements and scheduler reservations are labeled as different concepts and are never summed as if both were allocations.
The dashboard marks the all-on local budget unhealthy when physical GPU usage exceeds 14336 MiB or free VRAM drops below 2048 MiB.
NVIDIA telemetry failure degrades to an explicit unavailable state without failing the rest of the dashboard.
Windows WDDM per-process VRAM N/A is displayed as unavailable and never converted to zero.
Model state combines runtime provider status, service configuration and bounded scheduler leases; cloud models are marked remote and consume zero local model VRAM.
Polling runs only while the Resource Monitor page is active, prevents overlapping requests and keeps at most 60 chart samples and 100 in-memory model transitions.
The page is explanatory enough for a non-developer to distinguish loaded, configured, reserved and unavailable model states.
allowed_dependencies: Existing Python and Node standard libraries, existing Hina resource scheduler, Electron typed IPC and the fixed NVIDIA nvidia-smi executable; no new package dependency.
acceptance_criteria: GET /v1/resources/status returns bounded scheduler telemetry, active lease details and model/service state without secret or user-content fields.
Scheduler unit tests prove lease snapshots expose owner, reservation, priority, preemptibility and remaining TTL while expired leases are pruned.
Python unit tests prove robust bounded NVIDIA telemetry parsing while the desktop explicitly treats unavailable provider/process measurements as unknown rather than zero.
Electron unit tests prove bounded model load/unload transition history and desktop security tests prove resource IPC is operator-only.

The new Tài nguyên AI page updates approximately every 1.5 seconds only while visible and shows RAM, VRAM, GPU load, temperature, power, active leases, model state, transition history and a 60-sample trend.
The page visibly distinguishes physical use from reservation, explains cloud/local effects and reports a clear healthy, near-limit or headroom-violation analysis.
Desktop build/unit tests and narrow core-runtime resource route tests pass without retaining generated test artifacts.
required_test_commands: $env:PYTHONPATH='apps/core-runtime/src;packages/contracts/src;packages/safety-policy/src;packages/text-brain/src;workers/speech/src;workers/perception/src'; uv run --frozen python -m unittest discover -s packages/text-brain/tests -p "test_config_resource.py"; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { uv run --frozen python -m unittest discover -s apps/core-runtime/tests -p "test_resource_routes.py" }
